subject: use the 70% rule as a screen, not a verdict
preheader: a quick flip check that still needs deal-specific costs and targets.
headline: The 70% rule is a starting screen—not a universal Offer Ceiling.
body: A common quick screen is purchase ceiling = ARV × 0.70 − rehab cost. The retained spread is intended to absorb selling, financing, holding, contingency, and profit—but those amounts vary materially by deal.

Illustration only: at a $400,000 entered ARV and $60,000 entered rehab budget, the rule produces $220,000. That is not automatically the price you should pay; replace the factor and every cost assumption with figures for the property, financing, timeline, market, and your return target.

The useful lesson is not that 70% is magic. It is that a flip offer needs room for more than construction. Selling costs, interest, taxes, insurance, utilities, permits, delays, concessions, and contingency all compete for the spread.

TrueCap Pro models an Offer Ceiling from the ARV, rehab, holding, financing, selling-cost, and target inputs you enter. It is not a recommended offer and does not automatically supply property-specific ARV comps or a contractor rehab quote. Verify every material input before negotiating or offering.
